style_when: the story is regulatory or contractual — a filing, a mandate, a rate notice, a certificate, a purchase order that changed the economics
prompt: Overhead 90-degree flat-lay photograph on a brushed-steel desk in a control room: a single bone-white one-page scorecard form, faint grey printed rules, blank fields and empty checkbox rows, lying slightly askew across the frame's left third. Beneath its left corner a thin token-invoice printout; beneath its right edge the dense paper side of a thick contract-review stack bleeding off the right of frame. A heavy brushed-steel pen with a safety-yellow clip rests diagonally across the page, a soft shadow cast by diffused window light from the upper left. Graphite, bone white and safety-yellow palette, 50mm lens directly overhead, deep even focus, fine film grain, muted paper tones, generous negative space.
negative_prompt: garbled text, random lettering, legible numbers, watermark, logo
rationale: The story's protagonist is literally a written artefact — the one-page scorecard the surviving teams carry — so the document still life is the honest hero, not a metaphor. The top-down flat-lay lets the page act as the gate: the thin demo invoice beneath one corner, the heavy review stack beneath the other, the whole economics of the article weighed in one frame a reader names in three words.
subject: a blank one-page scorecard form bridging a thin token-cost printout and a thick human-review document stack
core_thesis: 95% of companies get no measurable return from generative AI pilots not because the models fail but because nothing written down decides graduation — the fix is a one-page scorecard, priced in labor hours, with a dated payback threshold a demo must clear before it earns production compute.
core_conflict: The cheap half of the bill (token inference cost shown on the demo dashboard) versus the expensive half (unmetered human review minutes inside the cost per resolved work-unit) — demo excitement renewed quarter after quarter against a written, dated payback gate.
composition: Extreme asymmetric top-down flat-lay: the scorecard page commands the left third, the review stack bleeds off the right edge, generous graphite negative space above
